items.title: The Better AI Gets, the Rustier You Get
items.summary: In episode 1029 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Katie Malone, Host of Linear Digressions about what keeping a human in the loop actually does to the human. Katie explains that as automation gets better, people naturally trust it more, become less experienced at handling the hard cases themselves and lose some of their expertise. She also points to a second failure mode for businesses: the efficiency gains from AI start to disappear if a human always has to oversee, approve and manage every step.

items.title: JitMem: Optimizing AI Memory at Read Time
items.summary: New Just-in-time AI Task-adaptive Memory Optimization by Salesforce. What if AI agents summarize their experience too early? What if skills are configurated only for a 1-dim representation? What if we miss out on the complexity of research results? What if an Ai compactifies data only on one axis? Salesforce’s new JitMem preserves raw trajectories and waits for the next task before an LLM curator extracts the relevant lessons for a frozen executor. We unpack how task-conditioned curation avoids premature information loss during compactification, why it makes memory optimization easier to train, and how the curator’s ability to generalize from past experience becomes the critical bottleneck. All rights w/ authors: Just-in-Time Memory: Learning to Curate Task-Adaptive Memory for LLM Agents Yefan Zhou*, Yang Li*, Zeyu Leo Liu, Semih Yavuz, Shafiq Joty from Salesforce AI Research {yefan.zhou,yli2,sjoty}@salesforce.com #airesearch #aitechnology #aiexplained
items.summary_html:
New Just-in-time AI Task-adaptive Memory Optimization by Salesforce. 

What if AI agents summarize their experience too early? What if skills are configurated only for a 1-dim representation? What if we miss out on the complexity of research results? What if an Ai compactifies data only on one axis? 

Salesforce’s new JitMem preserves raw trajectories and waits for the next task before an LLM curator extracts the relevant lessons for a frozen executor. 

We unpack how task-conditioned curation avoids premature information loss during compactification, why it makes memory optimization easier to train, and how the curator’s ability to generalize from past experience becomes the critical bottleneck.
